# Assigned question: generator-shortcuts

The strongest tested canonical-fitting rival is **count distinct nonzero colors,
then enlarge every cell by that count**, instead of counting all nonzero cells.
It matches all four canonical labeled pairs because their nonzero cells all have
distinct colors. This was independently checked on the current source, and is
also the hypothesis in prior audit `review-2b9742c54a64d33c:v0001`, which concerned
older source `4401f950f141d3f74df33c5664b285c19cbb9b638f1c835ba867a1cd14c4cad8`.

## Exact separating input and executed output

```json
[[4,4,0],[0,6,0],[0,0,6]]
```

This validator-accepted 3×3 input has four nonzero cells but two distinct nonzero
colors. The intended rule produces a **12×12** output by replacing every cell,
including each zero, with a 4×4 block. The rival produces **6×6**, using 2×2
blocks. The full input, both full outputs, and validation are retained in
`checks/canonical-shortcut/report.json`.

The exact supported `arcpuzzles apply` execution is retained in
`checks/canonical-shortcut/racket.json`. It executes canonical rule
`d959c287782b` against final generator
`9070d806a5720ecc39eae06c4294c338f5a7afb564e0c89ad36af898fbd6369f`.
All three retained cases have valid outputs, no Racket error, agreement between
the executed output and the independent Python mirror, and disagreement with
the rival. `checks/probe_shortcut.py` reproduces the canonical fit, inputs,
validator checks and receipt comparisons without hidden API imports.

## Does the generator emit separators?

Yes. The current generator emits repeated colors on ordinary paths. The retained
probe records an ordinary `generate(17, 0)` draw and an exact replay of the older
audit's override recipe: seed 123, sample index 7, medium difficulty, `grid_n=3`,
`n_cells=4`, `unique_colors=false`. Both current-source inputs pass `self_check`
and separate cell count from color count. Their actual generated grids and
Racket/rival outputs are in the same report. This establishes current behavior;
it does not rewrite the older audit's source-bound administrative status.

The existing three-step palette schedule puts repeated-color witnesses into
three-demo lessons. The required fresh Racket census materialized 100 lessons
per band: 300/300 production lessons refuted the declared rival, and 1,200/1,200
rotations had no declared-rival ambiguity. It materialized 1,200 pairs with 1,189
unique normalized inputs. The four-query research episode separately has three
demonstrations, four distinct queries and seven unique inputs, with the rival
refuted by demonstrations before all four queries are checked. See
`checks/lesson-census.json`, `checks/four-query.jsonl` and
`checks/four-query-validation.json`.

The ordinary repair in this return changes seed validation only; the established
repeated-color distribution is retained. The proposed parameter prototype also
provides repeated-color demonstrations, and treats color-count scaling as a
separate fixed episode setting with its own executed Racket program. Prototype
variants do not change canonical production labels.

These results concern the named plausible rival and the declared six-setting
prototype family. They do not prove that arbitrary alternative programs are
uniquely ruled out by finitely many demonstrations.
